'''Karl Edwin Gustafson''' <!-- (born May 7, 1935){{cn|date=June 2023}} --> is an American [[mathematician]]. Gustafson spent most of his career at the [[University of Colorado Boulder|University of Colorado]], [[Boulder, Colorado|Boulder]], in the Department of Mathematics. He is known for developing the [[antieigenvalue theory]] in [[applied mathematics]].

== Education and career ==
Gustafson received two [[Bachelor of Science]] degrees from the University of Colorado in 1958 (Engineering Physics/Applied Mathematics and Business Finance) before a PhD in Mathematics in 1965 from the [[University of Maryland, College Park|University of Maryland]].&nbsp;He performed post-doctoral work in Switzerland and Italy as a recipient of an NSF-NATO grant, held an assistant professor position at the [[University of Minnesota]], and then moved back to Colorado where he was Associate Professor and then Professor of Mathematics at the University of Colorado<ref>{{cite web|url=https://math.colorado.edu/~gustafs/newvita.pdf|title=Curriculum vitae|access-date=2024-06-12}}</ref> for over 50 years.&nbsp;He retired as Professor Emeritus in 2020.<ref>{{Cite web |date=September 29, 2016 |title=Karl Gustafson |url=https://www.colorado.edu/math/karl-gustafson |access-date=2022-04-30 |website=Department of Mathematics |language=en}}</ref>

== Scholarship ==
Gustafson published articles and books in many areas of mathematics, both applied and pure, and in physics and the mathematics of finance.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Gustafson |first=Karl |year=2022 |title=Karl Gustafson, Department of Mathematics |url=http://www.colorado.edu/math/karl-gustafson |access-date=April 27, 2022 |website=University of Colorado, Boulder}}</ref> Early in his career he developed the [[antieigenvalue theory]] in the area of applied mathematics.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Gustafson |first=Karl |year=1968 |title=The angle of an operator and positive operator products |journal=Bulletin of the American Mathematical Society |volume=74 |issue=3 |pages=488–492 |doi=10.1090/s0002-9904-1968-11974-3 |s2cid=121445437 |issn=0273-0979|doi-access=free }}</ref> He returned to this topic in 2012 with a book exploring how the theory applies in the contexts of [[numerical analysis]], wavelets, statistics, quantum mechanics, finance and optimization.<ref>{{Cite book |first=Karl |last=Gustafson |url=http://worldcat.org/oclc/921222071 |title=Antieigenvalue analysis : with applications to numerical analysis, wavelets, statistics, quantum mechanics, finance and optimization |date=2012 |publisher=World Scientific Pub. Co |isbn=978-981-4366-29-8 |oclc=921222071}}</ref> Gustafson wrote an introductory guide to partial differential equations (''Introduction to Partial Differential Equations and Hilbert Space Methods)'' that was published in three editions in the United States<ref>{{Cite book |last=E. |first=Gustafson, Karl |url=http://worldcat.org/oclc/310838854 |title=Partial differential equations and Hilbert space methods. |date=1980 |publisher=Wiley |isbn=0-471-04089-4 |oclc=310838854}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book |last=Gustafson |first=Karl |title=Introduction to Partial Differential Equations and Hilbert Space Methods, 2d edition |publisher=Wiley |year=1987 |location=New York |pages=438}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book |last=Gustafson |first=Karl |url=http://worldcat.org/oclc/246284657 |title=Partial Differential Equations and Hilbert Space Methods, 3d edition (revised) |publisher=Dover |year=1999 |isbn=0-486-61271-6 |location=New York |pages=472 |oclc=246284657}}</ref> and in various versions in three foreign countries.<ref>{{Cite book |last=Gustafson |first=Karl |title=Introduction to Partial Differential Equations and Hilbert Space Methods |publisher=Yeh Yeh Publishers |year=1983 |location=Taiwan |pages=285}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book |last=Gustafson |first=Karl |title=Applied Partial Differential Equations 1 and 2 |publisher=Kaigai |year=1991–1992 |location=Japan |pages=247 & 235}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book |last=Gustafson |first=Karl |title=Introduction to Partial Differential Equations and Hilbert Space Methods, 3d edition |publisher=International Journal Services |year=1993 |location=India |pages=460}}</ref> Gustafson also published academic books in other areas of mathematics<ref>{{Cite book |last=E. |first=Gustafson, Karl |url=http://worldcat.org/oclc/34912671 |title=Numerical range : the field of values of linear operators and matrices |date=1997 |publisher=Springer |isbn=0-387-94835-X |oclc=34912671}}</ref> and in related subjects such as [[quantum mechanics]]<ref>{{Cite book |last=Gustafson |first=Karl |title=Quantum Mechanics in Mathematics, Chemistry and Physics |publisher=Springer |year=1981 |location=New York |pages=506}}</ref> and [[fluid dynamics]].<ref>{{Cite book |last=Gustafson |first=Karl |title=Vortex Methods and Vortex Motion |publisher=SIAM |year=1991 |location=Philadelphia |pages=227}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book |last=Gustafson |first=Karl |title=Lectures on Computational Fluid Dynamics, Mathematical Physics, and Linear Algebra |publisher=Kaigai Publishers |year=1997 |location=Japan |pages=169}}</ref> In 2022, he became the honoree of an endowed faculty chair at the University of Colorado. The funds for the chair came from an anonymous donor who was a former student of Gustafson's. The chair will be known as the Karl Gustafson Endowed Chair of Quantum Engineering and will be embedded in the Department of Electrical, Computer and Energy Engineering within the College of Engineering and Applied Sciences, at Gustafson's request. Gustafson proposed that the chair be part of the College of Engineering in hopes that the faculty who hold the chair might have a "fundamental breakthrough in some way other than just writing papers," according to Gustafson.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Adams |first=Emily |date=February 1, 2022 |title=Honoree hopes new endowment will lead to quantum breakthrough |url=http://www.colorado.edu/engineering/2022/02/01/honoree-hopes-new-endowment-will-lead-to-quantum-breakthrough |access-date=April 27, 2022 |website=University of Colorado, Boulder, College of Engineering and Applied Science}}</ref>

== Other publications and pursuits ==
Gustafson also had many interests outside of academia. As a young rock climber in Colorado in the 1950s, Gustafson and colleagues were at the forefront of the sport of free climbing and completed several first ascents of local rock faces and mountain ridges in the area (North Face of The Matron, North Face of Schmoe's Nose and the Snowmass-Capitol Ridge).<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Gustafson |first=Karl |year=1952 |title=The Snowmass-Capitol Ridge |journal=Trail and Timberline (Colorado Mountain Club) |volume=404 |pages=119–121}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book |last1=Ament |first1=Pat |title=High Over Boulder |last2=McCarty |first2=Cleve |publisher=Two Lights Publishing |year=1995 |location=Boulder, Colorado |pages=81, 97}}</ref> Gustafson published a memoir in 2012, entitled ''The Crossing of Heaven'', which recounted, among other life experiences, more of his mountaineering adventures and his role in top-secret (at the time) military intelligence work during the Cold War, including writing the software in 1960 for the first US spy satellite.<ref>{{Cite book |last=E. |first=Gustafson, Karl |url=http://worldcat.org/oclc/828889966 |title=The crossing of heaven : memoirs of a mathematician |date=2012 |publisher=Springer |isbn=978-3-642-22558-1 |oclc=828889966}}</ref> After surviving a hemorrhagic stroke in 2016, Gustafson wrote a second memoir, ''Reverberations of a Stroke'', concerning his medical recovery and return to teaching mathematics at the university.<ref>{{Cite book |first=KARL |last=GUSTAFSON |url=http://worldcat.org/oclc/1164825312 |title=REVERBERATIONS OF A STROKE. |date=2020 |publisher=SPRINGER |isbn=978-3-030-12864-7 |oclc=1164825312}}</ref>
